Tomorrow the cycle carries on from its published branch, and the closing and Land come later.

"Land on main" would be a different experiment:
- **Branch backup** (the prompt as written): opening and config rung, agent commit with `--covers`, trailers, push. That's Todo **A mid-cycle backup**. The cycle stays open.
- **Land on main:** add the closing commit (`commit --closing`), then the Land. The Land itself commits the agent `@` with one `ochid:` per work commit, sets the links, merges and pushes, and `main` moves. That's Todo **A local cycle lands N:1**. In that case, drop the `commit -s a --covers` step, or you'd be testing N:M with two agent commits.

Both are useful. If you want it on the branch, use the prompt as I wrote it, with no "Land" in it.

content.text:
No. You don't need to say anything about the agent repo, and I'd avoid the word "Land" here altogether.

**"Land" has one meaning in the rules:** the sequence that makes a cycle permanent on the trunk (`[cycle] trunk`, `main` when absent). It means sync, the closing, merging onto `main`, publishing, and installing. "Land on the current branch" isn't a Land under the rules, so an agent reading it would have to guess. The step you want is a publish, or a backup, of the cycle's bookmark.

**The agent repo always goes to `main`.** It has no cycle bookmarks, and `main` is its only line. So any push of the agent side, whether `push -s b`, `push -s a` or a Land, moves the agent `main` to the agent commit. There's nothing to choose and nothing to say.

So for `wt5`, word it as a backup:

> …then back the cycle up without landing it: `commit -s a --covers 'main..@-'` …, `trailers --update`, `push -s b`, which publishes the work repo's cycle bookmark, leaving `main` where it is, and the agent repo's `main`.

That matches the prompt I gave you, with the parenthesis spelling out where each side goes.

> 2. Validate, flip the rung to (done), and commit it locally with `vc-x1-dev commit -s w`.
> 3. Back the cycle up without landing it, as one command line: `vc-x1-dev commit -s a --covers 'main..@-' --title "chore: configure this workspace" --body "<two paragraphs>" && vc-x1-dev trailers --update && vc-x1-dev push -s b`. This publishes the work repo's cycle bookmark, leaving `main` where it is, and the agent repo's `main`.
> 4. Check with `vc-x1-dev validate-desc -s b`.

When that's done, come back here for vc-x1's half. That's your go on the `--covers` rung, then the split, the script rung, the notes, and the push you confirm.

content.text:
It's doing well. It recorded the `&&` chain as a second bend without being asked, which is what "no rule bends silently" wants, and it dry-ran `--covers` and confirmed the two `ochid:` lines. My answers to its two questions, plus one fix:

1. **Run step 4 after the push, then "Published": yes.** `validate-desc` only reads, and you asked for it explicitly, so it's a requested exception, not a slip. It also means the check comes before you leave.
2. **`-r @-`: yes, but take three commits back** so the opening is checked too: `vc-x1-dev validate-desc -s b -r @- -n 3`. On the work side that's the rung, the opening, and the apply pair. On the agent side it's the new agent commit, the apply's agent commit, and the initial commit.
3. **The body isn't wrapped.** Each paragraph is one long line. Commit bodies are wrapped at 75 columns, and the apply pair had the same slip earlier. Ask it to wrap before running.

So your reply could be:

> Go with both, but make step 4 `vc-x1-dev validate-desc -s b -r @- -n 3`, and wrap the agent commit's body at 75 columns first.

content.text:
`validate-desc` does test the placeholder. The rule in `link_findings` (`src/validate_desc.rs:225-260`) depends on whether the agent commit the `ochid:` names exists yet:

| The partner (the last `ochid:`) is | `ocid:` holds | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| the uncommitted agent `@` | `xxxx` | `ok`, which is our state right now |
| the uncommitted agent `@` | a SHA | wrong: "ocid: has …, and … is the uncommitted agent @" |
| committed | `xxxx` | wrong: "ocid: placeholder, and … is committed at …" |
| committed | a SHA other than its own | wrong: "ocid: has …, and … is at …" |
| committed, but on no remote | its SHA | a note, not an error |

It also checks the `ocid:` URL against the agent repo's `origin`, and every `pcid:` against the commit's actual parents. So your run was correct: all six rungs name `qqvvzozm`, which is still the agent `@`, so `xxxx` is right for every one of them.

After the backup, the same check gets strict. If `trailers --update` were skipped, or missed a commit, each `xxxx` left would show as "placeholder, and qqvvzozm is committed at …". The check I'll run afterwards, `validate-desc -s b -r @- -n 8`, covers all six rungs plus the opening's parent on `main`.

The push command is unchanged and waiting for your go.
